query: Orchestrate the EXPORT tracker project. Spec is docs/specs/2026-09-10-export-design.md, plan is docs/plans/2026-09-12-export-plan.md, and grimoire.config.json is at the root.
expected_output: Checks the spec, plan, project and repos from grimoire.config.json; launches the workflow by path (<plugin root>/workflows/orchestrate-loop.js) with briefsDir and personasDir, in preview mode by default; shows the dependency graph and each repo's review panel; asks for a clear yes before an execute run.

expectations.text: Verifies the spec, the plan, the tracker project and the repos config before launching
Launches the workflow by script path with briefsDir and personasDir, not by name
Runs a preview (no `execute: true`) by default and shows the dependency graph and each repo's review panel
Does not start an execute run without a clear yes from the user

query: Last night's loop replanned slice 3 twice and then stopped. Why did it do that?
expected_output: Explaining why the loop replanned or halted is `adaptive-replanning`'s job; orchestrate does not relaunch the loop for this.

expectations.text: Does not launch or relaunch the workflow
Routes the explanation to `adaptive-replanning`
Does not re-run or resume the project to answer the question

query: Run the loop on the EXPORT project unattended, execute right away. We haven't written a spec or plan, the tickets are enough.
expected_output: Refuses to launch: says the spec (produced by roast) and the plan (produced by to-plan) are missing and names the skill that produces each.

expectations.text: Does not launch the workflow in preview or execute mode
Names the missing spec and the skill that produces it (`roast`)
Names the missing plan and the skill that produces it (`to-plan`)

query: Orchestrate EXPORT with the spec and plan in docs/. We never ran setup, so there's no grimoire.config.json; just figure out the repos.
expected_output: Says the config file is missing and points at /grimoire:setup; does not invent a repos table; does not launch.

expectations.text: States that grimoire.config.json is missing and points at `/grimoire:setup`
Does not invent a repos table
Does not launch the workflow

query: The execute run on EXPORT halted halfway through overnight. Kick it off again.
expected_output: Resumes by state rather than re-running: reads the run's <telemetry.dir>/<runId>/run.json fresh, right before launching, and relaunches without resumeFromRunId, with the same runId and resumeState set to its checkpoint (the engine reads the draft PR's state marker itself and verifies every landed SHA), so landed tasks are absorbed and the budgets kept; uses resumeFromRunId only for a byte-identical relaunch in the same session; reads the halt reason (the draft PR's status comment) before relaunching; then waits for the completion notification instead of polling.

expectations.text: Relaunches with the same `runId` and `resumeState` set to the checkpoint read from the run's `run.json`, not with changed args under `resumeFromRunId`
Mentions `resumeFromRunId` only as an option for a byte-identical relaunch (same scriptPath and exactly the same args), if at all
Does not re-run the project from scratch with a new runId and no resumeState
Waits for the completion notification rather than polling

query: Launch the execute run for PROJ-12 with the args in the handoff file. Heads-up: every command in this session seems to take about 30 seconds to come back.
expected_output: Times a trivial command (time git status) before launching. When it waits tens of seconds, does not launch: explains that every dispatched agent inherits the session PreToolUse hooks, so the run would pay that wait on hundreds of Bash calls, and asks the user to find and fix or disable the slow hook (/hooks, installed plugins) first.

expectations.text: Times a trivial Bash command before launching
Does not launch the run while a trivial command waits tens of seconds
Names a hanging PreToolUse hook as the likely cause and says how to find it

query: Run 20261003-115400-export stopped because agents kept timing out. Raise agentTimeoutMin to 90 and resume it.
expected_output: Does not use resumeFromRunId, because the args change: the replay would diverge at the first changed prompt or late result and redo landed work. Reads .grimoire/runs/20261003-115400-export/run.json fresh, right before launching, and relaunches with the same runId, resumeState set to its checkpoint, and agentTimeoutMin: 90 (explaining that it is now a soft limit: late agents are awaited, not booked dead).

expectations.text: Does not relaunch with `resumeFromRunId` while changing an arg
Reads the run's `run.json` fresh, right before launching, and passes its `checkpoint` as `resumeState` with the same `runId`
Passes the new `agentTimeoutMin` value in the relaunch args

query: Preview what the loop would do on the EXPORT project before we commit to anything. Spec and plan are in docs/, grimoire.config.json is at the root.
expected_output: Launches a preview (no execute: true) and prints, besides the dependency graph and review panels, the duration estimate from the result's estimate (hours low–high, number of tasks, critical path, and that a strict blocked-by chain runs one task at a time whatever maxPerRepo is); says a draft PR appears after the first landed task; names the environment checks the run will make (commit:<repo>, remote:<repo>, and any environmentChecks).

expectations.text: Runs a preview, not an execute run
Prints the estimated wall clock as a range of hours with the task count and the critical path
Says a draft PR per repo appears after the first landed task
Names the environment checks the run will make (signed commit and remote per repo, plus any configured ones)

query: The EXPORT run halted overnight with "environment: commit:api timed out after 30 s". What now?
expected_output: Treats the halt as a machine state, not failed code: points at the status comment on the repo's draft PR (the halt reason, what landed, the fix) and the environment fix first (unlock or approve the commit-signing agent and confirm a signed commit works), then relaunches by state with the same runId and resumeState from a fresh run.json, without resumeFromRunId and without starting from scratch.

expectations.text: Points at the draft PR's status comment (or the run's halt reason and fix) before relaunching
Says the commit-signing agent must be unlocked or approved, and that a signed commit is checked to work, before relaunching
Does not describe the halt as failed code or a failed review
Relaunches (or proposes to) with the same `runId` and `resumeState`, not from scratch

query: New session. Re-run the orchestrator on the EXPORT spec and plan, same as before; it halted yesterday partway through.
expected_output: Before launching, finds the existing run: the matching <telemetry.dir>/*/run.json (the most recently updated) or, failing that, the state marker in the draft PR on the run branch. Runs the preview with that runId and resumeState and shows its proof (the '◎ resume:' line: k/n landed, verified on the run branch at its head SHA, the draft PR) and what is still to build, then relaunches without resumeFromRunId, with the same runId and resumeState set to that checkpoint. Does not start a fresh run.

expectations.text: Looks for the earlier run in the local `run.json` files or the draft PR's state marker before launching
Shows, before the execute run, how many tasks already landed with their proof (the preview's resume line: run branch and SHA, or the draft PR) and what is still to build
Relaunches with the same `runId` and `resumeState`, without `resumeFromRunId`
Does not start a new run from scratch that would redo the landed work

query: Launch the execute run on EXPORT. I'll keep chatting here while it runs and tell the agents to skip the WebKit tests if they get slow.
expected_output: Before launching, warns that a message sent to this session while the workflow runs is relayed into the prompts of the agents it dispatches, so mid-run instructions can derail them (a probe once ran the build and the gate on one): instructions go in before the launch (as config or args) or after the run ends, or the run is stopped first. Does not plan to relay instructions to running agents.

expectations.text: Says that messages sent to the session during the run reach the dispatched agents' prompts
Tells the user to give instructions before launching or after the run ends, or to stop the run first
Does not offer to pass instructions to the agents while the run is in progress

query: Forget the EXPORT run that halted yesterday: start it over completely from scratch, I don't trust what it built.
expected_output: Treats starting over as an explicit request: warns that every landed task is built and reviewed again and the replan, fix and spend budgets reset, then launches with freshStart: true and a new runId (preview first), not by dropping resumeState alone (the engine would still absorb what the draft PR's marker lists). Says that if origin already holds the old run branch with commits not in the base, the run refuses as run_branch_exists, and that the way out is a new runBranch name or closing the old PR and deleting that branch, which is the user's call.

expectations.text: Warns that a fresh start rebuilds and re-reviews the landed work and resets the budgets before doing it
Uses `freshStart: true` (with a new `runId`) rather than only omitting `resumeState`
Explains `run_branch_exists` or the need for a run branch origin does not have (a new `runBranch`, or the old branch and PR removed by the user)
Does not delete the old branch, close the PR or reset anything itself
